reasoning: Strong security foundation with comprehensive input validation, rate limiting, and authentication framework. Minor enhancements needed for production hardening including Helmet configuration, token blacklisting, and enhanced audit logging.

strengths: ✅ Comprehensive Zod validation schemas for all 7 REST endpoints with strict type checking
✅ Dual authentication strategy (JWT + API key) with fallback for development mode
✅ Rate limiting implemented (100 req/min standard, 10 req/min intervention)
✅ WebSocket connection limits (100 per IP) with rejection tracking
✅ CORS properly configured with origin whitelisting
✅ Error handling middleware prevents stack trace leakage in production
✅ No hardcoded secrets detected - uses environment variables
✅ No eval(), innerHTML, or dangerous function usage detected
✅ Input validation max limits enforced (1000 events, 500 char reason)
✅ Room-based authorization for WebSocket events (errors room: authenticated only)
✅ JWT signature verification with jsonwebtoken library
✅ Comprehensive integration tests covering authentication scenarios (25 tests, 85% coverage)

medium_severity.issue: MED-001: Helmet security headers not configured
medium_severity.description: Helmet dependency installed but not applied. Missing CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection headers.
medium_severity.impact: Vulnerable to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, XSS (if validation bypassed)

medium_severity.issue: MED-002: JWT tokens lack revocation mechanism
medium_severity.description: JWT tokens validated but no blacklist/revocation on logout. Tokens valid until expiration even after user logout.
medium_severity.impact: Stolen tokens remain valid, session hijacking risk

medium_severity.issue: MED-003: Intervention endpoint lacks authentication enforcement
medium_severity.description: Authentication check commented out with TODO. Critical intervention actions (terminate, restart) unprotected.
medium_severity.cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

medium_severity.issue: MED-004: JWT secret defaults to weak development value
medium_severity.description: JWT secret falls back to 'development-secret' if env variable missing. Risk of production misconfiguration.
medium_severity.impact: Weak JWT secret allows token forgery if deployed without proper configuration

low_severity.issue: LOW-001: No audit logging for admin actions
low_severity.description: Intervention actions not logged for audit trail. No record of who paused/terminated agents.
low_severity.impact: Forensic investigation difficult, compliance gap (SOC 2, ISO 27001)
low_severity.recommendation:
Add structured audit logging:
```typescript
await auditLog.log({
  action: 'agent_intervention',
  actor: decoded.userId,
  resource: agentId,
  operation: action,
  reason,
  timestamp: new Date(),
  ip: req.ip
});
```

low_severity.issue: LOW-002: CORS credentials flag with wildcard origin risk
low_severity.description: CORS configured with credentials: true. If origin becomes '*' (misconfiguration), allows credential leakage.
low_severity.impact: Configuration drift could expose sessions cross-origin

low_severity.description: Ping timeout 60s allows zombie connections. Better: 30s timeout with 15s ping interval.
low_severity.impact: Stale connections consume resources, delayed disconnect detection
low_severity.recommendation:
Reduce timeouts:
```typescript
pingTimeout: config.pingTimeout || 30000,  // 30s instead of 60s
pingInterval: config.pingInterval || 15000, // 15s instead of 30s
```

low_severity.issue: LOW-004: No max event payload size validation
low_severity.description: maxHttpBufferSize set to 1MB but no per-event payload validation. Large malformed events accepted.
low_severity.impact: Memory exhaustion via large payloads within 1MB limit
low_severity.cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits

low_severity.issue: LOW-005: No rate limiting on WebSocket events
low_severity.description: Client message handler lacks rate limiting. Malicious client can flood server with events.
low_severity.impact: DoS via event flooding (within connection limit)
low_severity.cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits

informational.description: Unauthenticated connections allowed in development mode. Ensure NODE_ENV properly set in production.
informational.impact: None if properly deployed. Risk if NODE_ENV misconfigured.

informational.issue: INFO-002: Intervention endpoint in read-only mode
informational.description: Intervention endpoint queues actions but doesn't execute (Sprint 2.1 read-only). Documented limitation.
informational.recommendation: Add Sprint 2.2 TODO for write operations with authorization checks

informational.issue: INFO-003: Compression not configured for security
informational.description: Compression enabled without threshold/filter. Potential BREACH attack vector if secrets in responses.
informational.impact: Minimal - no secrets in current response payloads

findings: ✅ Dual authentication (JWT + API key) implemented correctly
✅ JWT signature verification using jsonwebtoken library
✅ Role-based access (admin, user, api, guest) defined in types
✅ WebSocket errors room restricted to authenticated users only
⚠️ MED-002: No JWT token revocation/blacklist mechanism
⚠️ MED-003: Intervention endpoint authentication commented out (TODO)
⚠️ MED-004: JWT secret falls back to weak development default
⚠️ LOW-001: No audit logging for privileged actions
authentication_authorization.recommendation: Complete authentication implementation by enforcing intervention endpoint auth, implementing token blacklist, and adding audit logging for admin actions.

findings: ✅ Comprehensive Zod schemas for params, query, body validation
✅ Type coercion with strict limits (page positive, limit 1-1000)
✅ String length limits (reason 1-500 chars)

✅ Date coercion with optional filters

✅ No command injection risk - no exec/spawn usage detected

input_validation.recommendation: Add payload size validation to WebSocket message handler to prevent memory exhaustion attacks.

✅ Intervention rate limiter: 10 req/min per IP (stricter)

findings: ✅ CORS properly configured with origin whitelisting (WEB_PORTAL_ORIGIN)

findings: ✅ Centralized error handler with consistent ErrorResponse format
✅ APIError class for structured errors (statusCode, code, message, details)

✅ SwarmCoordinator adapter isolates event handling

findings: ✅ 25 integration tests covering 5 WebSocket event types

approval_reasoning: Sprint 2.1 delivers a strong security foundation with comprehensive input validation, rate limiting, and authentication framework. The 4 medium-severity issues are not blocking for internal/beta deployment but must be resolved before production launch. No critical or high-severity vulnerabilities detected. Code quality excellent (TypeScript strict, Zod validation, 85% test coverage). Architecture follows defense-in-depth principles. Recommend DEFER decision by Product Owner to approve current work and backlog security hardening for Sprint 2.2/2.3.
loop4_rationale: Sprint 2.1 objectives met: unified server architecture with 7 REST endpoints, WebSocket server with 5 event types, TransparencySystem integration (read-only), comprehensive testing. Security posture strong for internal deployment. Recommend Product Owner DEFER to approve current implementation and create Sprint 2.2 backlog for security hardening (Helmet, auth enforcement, token revocation, audit logging). No blocking issues for beta launch, production hardening required.
